 Beth Mooney had never missed a Big Bash game, but when she was forced to sit out against the Thunder, Mikayla Friday was happy to take the gloves
 Mikayla Friday says while taking the wicketkeeping gloves in place of Beth Mooney was "a bit nerve-wracking", her late call-up was equally a dream come true after helping maintain the Perth Scorchers' unbeaten start to Weber WBBL|12.
 Thursday's match against the Thunder at the WACA Ground was the first Mooney had ever missed across her 159-game career with the Heat and Scorchers, leaving Perth looking for a fill-in behind the stumps.
 Valiant Knight no match for stellar undefeated Scorchers 
 Friday, nee Hinkley, had never previously kept wicket in her 84 Big Bash games, but grabbed the opportunity. She did not have to wait long to be in the thick of the action, cleanly taking a skied chance off Georgia Voll in the first over of the match.
 "It was a bit nerve-wracking taking the gloves out there today," Friday said post-game. "I had so much fun out there.
 "I was sad for Moons, losing our leader, losing one of the best players in the world is not great news.
 "But on the other hand, it was pretty exciting ... I got to do a quick keeping session yesterday before the game, and I just felt really fortunate that I got that opportunity to take the gloves.
 "It doesn't come around, ever. Younger me would have would have been drooling at the fact that I got to keep at the WACA, it was something that I used to watch Adam Gilchrist do, and the young me inside is screaming and so excited at that opportunity.
 "Hopefully we get Moons back soon though, she's certainly a bit better than me, but it was an absolute dream."
 Friday entered WBBL|12 with confidence after a strong Spring Challenge campaign batting in the top-order, where she was the third-highest run-scorer hitting 176 runs in five innings at a strike rate of 135.38.
 That included a knock of 57 from 37 deliveries against the Strikers at Bankstown Oval.
 Coming in at No.5 in WBBL|12, the 28-year-old was not required to bat in Perth's opening game of the tournament, then was dismissed for three against the Stars before helping ice a win over the Thunder with 1no at Drummoyne Oval.
 Wareham content with middle-order role as Sixers loom 
 Given greater opportunity in their two more recent outings however, Friday has made an impact, hitting an unbeaten 24 from 19 against the Stars at North Sydney Oval, while her 24 off 16 helped seal victory over the Thunder on Wednesday night.
 "It's good to watch some of the world's best batters in front of me do their thing, and then I just go in and try and take a bit of the pressure off them," Friday said. "Feeling pretty good, you've got to take your chances when you get them, especially when we've got such a strong top order."
 The Scorchers are now 5-0 at the midway point of their regular season and in a strong position to claim a spot in the top four.
 They next host the Strikers on Saturday night, with Friday, who was part of the Thunder's title-winning team in WBBL|01, and the Heat side that won WBBL|05, reinforcing the importance of not getting ahead of themselves.
 "To be five from five now is awesome," she said. "It's probably not many times you get to start off five from five, and I certainly haven't been in a team that's done that.
 "(The belief) is really high. We're really excited at the start that we've gotten, but it is important to stay pretty level in this competition.
 "T20 cricket changes so quickly, as we know. So you don't want to ride the highs too much.
 "You want to try and stay pretty balanced because we're going to have to problem solve more and more as the tournament goes on."
